questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following vitamins cannot be stored in the body?
questions.solution:
Vitamins are classified into two groups depending upon their solubility in water or fat.

Fat soluble vitamins: Vitamins which are soluble in fat and oils but insoluble in water are kept in this group. These are vitamins A, D, E and K. They are stored in liver and adipose (fat storing) tissues.

Water soluble vitamins: B group vitamins and vitamin C are soluble in water. Water soluble vitamins must be supplied regularly in diet because they are readily excreted in urine and cannot be stored (except vitamin B12) in our body.

questions.solution:
The order of ionization enthalpy of elements of 2nd period in long form of periodic table is Li<B<Be<C<O<N<F<Ne.

Generally, on going left to right in a period, ionization energy increases, but there are some exceptions to this. For example, Be has more ionization energy than B, due to fulfilled s-orbital. And N has more ionization energy than O due to half filled p-subshell. 

So,In second period of the long form of the periodic table, the element B has second lowest first ionization enthalpy and element F has second highest first ionization enthalpy values.

questions.q:
The crystal filed theory is successful in explaining which of the following?

I. Ligands as point charges;

II. Formation and structures of complexes.

III. colour;

IV. Magnetic properties:

V . covalent character of metal-ligand bonding.
questions.solution: The crystal field theory (CFT) is an electrostatic model which considers the metal-ligand bond to be ionic arising purely from electrostatic interactions between the metal ion and the ligand. Ligands are treated as point charges in case of anions or point dipoles in case of neutral molecules. The colour in the coordination compounds can be readily explained in terms of the crystal field theory. However, the crystal field model is successful in explaining the formation, structures, colour and magnetic properties of coordination compounds to a large extent. However, from the assumptions that the ligands are point charges, it follows that anionic ligands should exert the greatest splitting effect.

Diamond, graphite and C60 are known as allotropes of carbon. In diamond, each carbon atom is tetrahedrally bonded to four carbon atoms, forming a 3-D network of strong,  covalently bonded carbon atoms. All carbon atoms are sp3 hybridized.

options: Random experiment consists of a sequence of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> identical trials
Each outcome can be referred to as a success or a failure
The probabilities of the two outcomes can change from one trial to the next
questions.solution:
We know that properties of Binomial Distribution are

  • There are two possible outcomes: true or false, success or failure, yes or no.
  • There is 'n' number of independent trials or a fixed number of $n$ times repeated trials.
  • The probability of success or failure remains the same for each trial.
  • Only the number of success is calculated out of n independent trials.
  • Every trial is an independent trial, which means the outcome of one trial does not affect the outcome of another trial.

So, the probabilities of the two outcomes can change from one trial to the next is not a property.

Assertion (A): In a region of constant potential, the electric field is zero and there can be no charge inside the region.

Reason (R): According to Gauss law. charge inside the region should be zero if electric field is zero.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true: (R) is correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true; (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
For Assertion,

Potential difference is given by dV=-E→·dr→, If E→ is zero, the potential will remain constant.

For Reason,

If in a region electric field is zero, net flux through any closed surface in that region will be zero. Therefore, if electric field is zero, according to Gauss's law the charge inside the region should be zero. Therefore, reason statement is correct, but it does not explain why the potential is constant.

Statement (A): Inside a charged hollow metal sphere, E=0, V≠0. (E- electric field, V-eslectric potential)

Statement (B): The work done in moving a positive charge on an equipotential surface is zero.

Statement (C): When two like charges are brought closer, their mutual electrostatic potential energy will increase.
options: A,B are true, C is false
A,C are true, B is false
B,C are true, A is false
questions.solution:
Inside a charged hollow, sphere electric field is constant. Now,

dV=-E→·dr→ therefore, dV=0 hence V is constant and not zero.

Potential difference is defined as the work done in moving per unit charge in moving it from one point to other. Therefore, work done in moving a charge on an equipotential surface is zero.

When two like charges are brought closer, work is done against electrostatic force. Therefore, their mutual electrostatic potential energy increases.

Hence, all the three statements are correct.

questions.solution:
Dot/Scalar product of two vectors gives scalar result. Cross/Vector product will give vector result.

Case: A→·A→B→·C→

Both left & right part will be a scalar value and hence its product will also be a scalar value.

Case: A→×B→·B→×C→

Both left and right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo dot product and the result will be a scalar value.

Case: A→×C→×B→×C→

Both left and right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo cross product and the result will be a vector value.

Case: A→×B→×C→

Both left and right part will be a vector, and then these two vectors will undergo cross product and the result will be a vector value.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Consider the statements
In a semi conductor
(A) There are no free electrons at 0 K.
(B) There are no free electrons at any temperature
(C) The number of free electrons increases with temperature,
(D) The number of free electrons is less than that in a conductor.
options: B,C,D are true but A is false
A,B,C are true but D is false
A,C,D are true but B is false.
A,B,C and D are all true.
questions.solution:
In a semiconductor, at 0 K all the electrons are in the valence band and no electrons are there in the conduction band. At 0 K there are no free electrons but the number of electrons increases with the increase in temperature. As the temperature increases electrons gain kinetic energy, thus, breaks the covalent bonds and move to conduction band as the result number of free electrons and holes increases.The number of free electrons are less as they form a covalent bonds due to which lattice structure is created.

So, A,C,D are true but B is false.

The path consists of (i) an isothermal expansion of work <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>, (ii) an adiabatic expansion and (iii) an isothermal expansion of work <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. questions.solution:
Internal energy is a state function and the change in the internal energy is zero for isothermal process.

In the given information, two processes are isothermal and one process is adiabatic. Therefore, the net change in the internal energy is equal to the change in the internal energy during the adiabatic process. Therefore,

∆Uadiabatic=-30 J

For adiabatic process ∆Q=0. Therefore,

∆Uadiabatic=-Wadiabatic⇒Wadiabatic=30 J

One newton is therefore the force needed to accelerate one kilogram of mass at the rate of one metre per second squared in the direction of the applied force. A newton is defined as 1 kg m s-2.
